messages:
maria nguyen: heads up, onboarding sampleapp started spiking 429s after yesterday's auth refresh patch

samir patel: huh, which path? prefetch or straight pagination?

maria nguyen: prefetch + pagination. we warm cursors (10 each) on signin. when STS rotated some inflight requests got 401 -> retried by SDK immediately -> those retries counted as fresh inflight tokens and blew past the client limiter

leo.bot: alert: sampleapp-onboard-prewarm: 10.2k 429s in 45s (region-us-east-1) :rotating_light:

samir patel: can you paste a snippet of the client logs? curious if retry backoff is in place

maria nguyen: logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:01Z] prefetcher: start cursor=abc token_id=ststmp1
[2026-03-15T10:12:01Z] http: GET /v1/embeds status=401 token=ststmp1
[2026-03-15T10:12:01Z] sdk-retry: retry attempt=1 reason=auth_refresh token=ststmp2
[2026-03-15T10:12:01Z] limiter: inflight=34 limit=32 action=throttle status=429
[2026-03-15T10:12:01Z] prefetcher: cursor=def token_id=ststmp2 status=queued
```

cassandra li: sounds like a token-swap race. SDK immediately swaps token and retries, but the retry is treated as new work by the local windowing code. we don't have de-dup or transient counting for auth-sourced retries

samir patel: i can reproduce locally. minimal repro: spawn 8 prefetch workers, force auth refresh on first request, immediate retry -> clients hit leaky-window fast. js snippet: 
```
// repro.js
const fetch = async () => {
  // simulate 401 then instant token swap
  if (Math.random() < 0.3) throw { status: 401 }
  return 'ok'
}

async function worker() {
  try { await fetch() } catch (e) { if (e.status===401) await fetch() }
}

Promise.all(new Array(8).fill(0).map(()=>worker()))
```

maria nguyen: note: sampleapp prefetch config uses window=10 concurrent per user. quick mitigation is to drop this to 3 until SDK patch lands

cassandra li: long term we should: 1) treat auth-retries as transient and don't increment the concurrency quota until the attempt receives a non-401 response OR 2) add a request fingerprint cache so retries within Xs are deduped client-side

samir patel: agreed. i'll open a tiny PR to make auth-retries use a short hold slot (count after success). also adding an opt-in flag `prefetch_dedupe` for the sampleapp

deploy-bot: canary deploy requested: prefetch_dedupe=true to sampleapp-staging by @samir patel

maria nguyen: thanks! also adding a note to the onboarding doc: "if you see sudden 429s after auth rotation, reduce prefetch window or enable prefetch_dedupe"

leo.bot: reaction :thumbsup: from 3 users

samir patel: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/458 quick patch + tests. leaving follow-up to add fingerprint cache.

maria nguyen: will update the sampleapp config this afternoon and monitor. if anyone sees residual 429s ping me here

cassandra li: filing an internal issue to track SDK parity: how other language SDKs handle auth-retry counting vs go/js

maria nguyen: sounds good. nice catch by the monitoring alerts :eyes:
